clears) |\n| `PATCH .../eval-suites/{suiteId}/schedule` | Enable/disable scheduled runs; `environmentId` pins which environment t
hey launch |\n| `GET .../eval-runs/{runId}` | Run status, result, and summary; poll until terminal. Carries `gateWaiver`: the audi
ted override in force over this run's gate, or `null` |\n| `GET .../eval-runs/{runId}/gate` | The stored suite quality-gate report
for this run (`passed` / `failed` / `non_gateable` / `not_configured`). `not_configured` is a 200 report, never a missing route |
\n| `GET .../eval-runs/{runId}/decision-summary` | **Start here when a run did not pass.** The canonical run decision contract: th
e verdict and where it came from, counts labelled with the population they count, the run's own verdict decision, and per-trial di
agnostics with the user-value chain, the first failed stage, the failure category, evidence scoped to that stage, and one next act
ion (paginated) |\n| `POST .../eval-runs/{runId}/gate-waivers` | Override a **failing** run's release gate until `expiresAt` (requ
ired, future, max 30 days out), with a `reason` (required, max 500 chars). Manage tier. Does NOT change the run's `result`; the ru
n keeps its verdict and the waiver is reported alongside it. `409` when one is already in force, returning the existing waiver |\n
| `GET .../eval-runs/{runId}/gate-waivers` | The waiver in force over a run, or `null`. Readable by anyone who can view the run |\
n| `DELETE .../eval-runs/{runId}/gate-waivers/{waiverId}` | Revoke a waiver, putting the gate back. Idempotent; a second call repo
rts the original revocation rather than restamping it |\n| `GET .../eval-runs/{runId}/iterations` | Per-iteration results: tool ca
lls, token usage, latency (paginated) |\n| `GET .../eval-runs/{runId}/iterations/{iterationId}/trace` | Full trace: messages + exp

ected-vs-actual analysis |
| `GET .../eval-suites/{suiteId}/runs` | Recent runs for a suite, newest first |

**Eval result inge
stion** (`/projects/{projectId}/eval-ingest/...`): how `@mcpjam/sdk` saves results from eval runs executed outside the platform (l
ocal dev, CI). The `{projectId}` segment accepts the literal `default` for the key org's Default project. Most users never call th
ese directly; set `MCPJAM_API_KEY` and the [SDK reporter](https://docs.mcpjam.com/sdk/concepts/saving-results.md) does:\n\n| Endpo
int | What it does |\n| - | - |\n| `POST .../eval-ingest/report` | One-shot: create a run from finished results and finalize it |\
n| `POST .../eval-ingest/runs/start` | Chunked flow: create (or idempotently reuse) a run by `externalRunId` |\n| `POST .../eval-i
ngest/runs/iterations` | Append an iteration batch to a started run |\n| `POST .../eval-ingest/runs/finalize` | Finalize a chunked
run (idempotent) |\n| `POST .../eval-ingest/artifacts` | Store one artifact's raw bytes (widget HTML too large to send inline) an
d return its `storageId` |\n| `POST .../eval-ingest/artifacts/upload-url` | Retired. Answers `410 Gone` with `details.code: \"SDK_
UPGRADE_REQUIRED\"`. `@mcpjam/sdk` 8.17.0 and later upload artifacts with `POST .../eval-ingest/artifacts` instead |\n\n**Agent**

(`/projects/{projectId}/agent`): a headless assistant turn for
building conversational surfaces:

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |\n| `POST .../agent` | Run ONE assistant turn over a `messages` history (`{role: \"user\"\\|\"assistant\", content}` item
s, max 50 messages × 8 KB each, 96 KB total). The model is pinned server-side and billed to the project. The turn can read project
servers/suites/runs and **create eval suites**; it can NOT start runs: kick those off yourself with `POST .../eval-runs`. Respond
s synchronously with `reply`, the `toolCalls` it made, `createdResources` (ids + app links), and token `usage`. Capped at 4 concur
rent turns per organization and \\~90 s wall clock. **Not idempotent; never blind-retry**: dedupe on your own trigger identity, an
d on an error response check `details.createdResources` (and, after a lost response, list suites) before retrying, or you'll creat

e duplicates |

**Studies** (`/projects/{projectId}/studies...`):

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |
| `GET .../studies`
| List the project's published studies: name, access mode, attached servers, share link |\n| `GET .../studies/{studyId}` | One st
udy's full read: model, system prompt, tool-approval policy, resolved servers, the environment it publishes, and its insights enve
lope. The last two need workspace membership and are **absent** for a share-link visitor, never null |\n\n**Swarms, authoring** (`
/projects/{projectId}/personas...`, `.../goals...`,\n`.../swarms...`): the definitions a swarm run executes. A **persona** is a\nr
eusable synthetic character; a **goal** is the task you point one at; a\n**swarm** is an authoring container holding defaults for

the goals made
under it. Nothing here starts anything; launching is
`POST .../goals/{goalId}/runs`.

| Endpoint | What it does

|
| - | - |
| `GET .../personas` | List the project's personas |
| `POST .../personas` | Create a persona (accepts `Idempotenc
y-Key`) |\n| `GET .../personas/{personaId}` | One persona |\n| `PATCH .../personas/{personaId}` | Update a persona. Goals referenc
e it by id, so renaming is safe |\n| `DELETE .../personas/{personaId}` | Delete a persona. **409** while goals still reference it
|\n| `GET .../goals` | List the project's goals |\n| `POST .../goals` | Create a goal (accepts `Idempotency-Key`). `personaId` and
`swarmId` must be in this project |\n| `GET .../goals/{goalId}` | One goal |\n| `PATCH .../goals/{goalId}` | Update a goal. `null
` CLEARS `environmentIds`; `iterations` and `maxTurns` must be sent together |\n| `DELETE .../goals/{goalId}` | **Archive** a goal
; existing runs keep pointing at the definition they executed |\n| `GET .../swarms` | List swarm containers |\n| `POST .../swarms`
| Create a swarm container (accepts `Idempotency-Key`) |\n| `GET .../swarms/{swarmId}` | One swarm |\n| `PATCH .../swarms/{swarmI
d}` | Update the container's defaults. Not a cascade; existing goals keep their own values |\n| `DELETE .../swarms/{swarmId}` | **
Archive** a swarm. The goals under it stay launchable |\n\n**Swarms, generation**. Drafts a model writes for you. Both routes retu
rn\ncandidates and **persist nothing**: feed what you want to keep to the create\nroutes above. Neither accepts an `Idempotency-Ke

y`, and retries return
different drafts.

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |
| `POST .../personas/generate` | Draft a slat
e of personas (and goals for each) grounded in a server attachment or an environment |\n| `POST .../goals/generate` | Draft goals

for a persona passed **by value**, so you can draft before you save |

> [!WARNING]
>
> The generation routes consume **no cus
tomer credits** (the model cost is on\n> MCPJam). They are still subject to usage limits, and each limit means a\n> different wait
: a per-minute burst brake (`429`, retry in seconds), your\n> organization's daily generation quota (`429`, resets at UTC midnight
), and\n> MCPJam's own daily budget for the feature (`429` with\n> `details.code: \"platform_capacity\"`, resets at UTC midnight).
All three carry\n> `Retry-After`. Honor it rather than guessing. `details.canTopUp` is `false`\n> on every one: buying credits do

es not lift them, so do not retry in a loop
> or switch identities to get around them.

**Swarms, runs** (`/projects/{projectId

}/goals/{goalId}/runs`,
`.../goal-runs/...`): launching a goal and reading what it produced:

| Endpoint | What it does |
| -
| - |\n| `GET .../goals/{goalId}/runs` | That goal's runs, newest first |\n| `POST .../goals/{goalId}/runs` | **Launch.** Answers
`202`; the fan-out has started, not finished. Send `Idempotency-Key`. Optional `expectedSponsored` is how many conversations you e
xpect MCPJam to sponsor; a different actual split is a `409` (`details.code: swarm_funding_changed`) and nothing is created. The r
esponse can report `funding` (`sponsored`, `credits`, `total`) |\n| `GET .../goal-runs/{runId}` | The full run: counts, per-target
breakdown, per-session `attempts` |\n| `GET .../goal-runs/{runId}/sessions` | The chat sessions the run produced (summaries, not
transcripts) |\n| `POST .../goal-runs/{runId}/cancel` | Stop a run. Idempotent; a second cancel is `200` with `alreadyCanceled: tr

ue`, not a `409` |

Three things worth knowing before you write the client:

* **Always send `Idempotency-Key` on a launch.**
